definitions.rationale: This is the base equation of the named mathematical summary oddDigitProduct: with no remaining digits, it returns the accumulator.
This is the positive-input recurrence for oddDigitProduct, decomposing N into parity, decimal quotient, decimal digit, and accumulator arguments for oddDigitStep.
definitions.text:
rule oddDigitProduct(N:Int, A:Int)
    => oddDigitStep(
         pyMod(N, 2) ==Int 1,
         (N -Int pyMod(N, 10)) /Int 10,
         pyMod(N, 10),
         A)
    requires N >Int 0

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the oddDigitStep case in which the current digit is not odd, preserving the accumulator and continuing with the quotient.
definitions.text:
rule oddDigitStep(B:Bool, Q:Int, _:Int, A:Int)
    => oddDigitProduct(Q, A)
    requires notBool B

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the oddDigitStep case for the first odd digit, replacing the zero sentinel accumulator with that digit.
definitions.text:
rule oddDigitStep(B:Bool, Q:Int, D:Int, 0)
    => oddDigitProduct(Q, D)
    requires B

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the oddDigitStep case for a later odd digit, multiplying it into a nonzero accumulator.
definitions.text:
rule oddDigitStep(B:Bool, Q:Int, D:Int, A:Int)
    => oddDigitProduct(Q, A *Int D)
    requires B andBool A =/=Int 0

source_rules.rationale: This simplifier asserts the non-odd-digit recurrence as an equality fact used during target comparison; it was present in verification.k before kprove ran and has no separate Stage 1 proof against a module omitting it.
source_rules.text:
rule {
    oddDigitProduct(
      (N -Int ((N %Int 10 +Int 10) %Int 10)) /Int 10,
      A)
    #Equals
    oddDigitProduct(N, A)
  } => true
    requires N >Int 0
     andBool pyMod(N, 2) =/=Int 1
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: This simplifier asserts the first-odd-digit recurrence for a zero accumulator; Stage 1 trusted it in the compiled verification definition rather than first proving its exact statement without the rule.
source_rules.text:
rule {
    oddDigitProduct(
      (N -Int ((N %Int 10 +Int 10) %Int 10)) /Int 10,
      (N %Int 10 +Int 10) %Int 10)
    #Equals
    oddDigitProduct(N, 0)
  } => true
    requires N >Int 0
     andBool pyMod(N, 2) ==Int 1
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: This simplifier asserts the later-odd-digit multiplication recurrence for a nonzero accumulator; it was available to the Stage 1 proof from compilation onward and was not separately established.
source_rules.text:
rule {
    oddDigitProduct(
      (N -Int ((N %Int 10 +Int 10) %Int 10)) /Int 10,
      A *Int ((N %Int 10 +Int 10) %Int 10))
    #Equals
    oddDigitProduct(N, A)
  } => true
    requires N >Int 0
     andBool A =/=Int 0
     andBool pyMod(N, 2) ==Int 1
    [simplification]
